title: Escarpment and Passage
premise: Quentin Hartwell, a salvage diver who has spent fifteen years erasing herself from every record that matters, is hired by her old rival Mara Kessler to raise a sealed strongbox from the Vespera, a wreck the navy forbids anyone to touch. The box holds proof of a wartime cover-up that could clear Quentin's brother's name—or bury her with it. As the monsoon closes in and the navy's fixers close in faster, Quentin must choose between the invisible life she built and the belonging she abandoned. In the end, she gives up the box to save her crew, but keeps the one thing no one can confiscate: the truth, spoken aloud, and a place among people who finally know who she is.
about_author: Ivo Vane is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade working coastal salvage before turning to writing. They live somewhere on the Atlantic seaboard and refuse, on principle, to say exactly where.

chapters.title: Fathoms of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. On a routine salvage job off a nameless cay, Quentin dives a rusting freighter and reflects on fifteen years of living under borrowed names, measured in nautical miles. Her crew—engineer Dov and deckhand Suri—are the only family she allows herself. Emotional beat: contentment built on deliberate forgetting, and the first tremor of unease when a navy patrol boat lingers too long nearby.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Dock
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Mara Kessler, Quentin's rival from their academy days, appears at a port bar with a contract: recover a sealed strongbox from the Vespera, a wreck officially struck from naval records. Quentin refuses—the job was sworn off after her brother's court-martial—but Mara reveals she knows Quentin's real name. Emotional beat: old resentment colliding with fear; invisibility was always a lease, not a deed.

chapters.title: Terms of Water
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Desperate for money after engine repairs drain their accounts, Quentin negotiates: they take the contract, but Mara comes aboard as client, not commander. Dov objects; Suri quietly sides with Quentin. Flashbacks surface of the night her brother Elias took the fall for a captain's orders. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment, the crew's trust tested before the lines are even cast.

chapters.title: Down to the Vespera
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. First dive on the forbidden wreck. Quentin finds the strongbox welded into the officer's quarters—and evidence someone else has been diving here recently, cutting fresh marks into the hull. A navy hydrophone buoy drifts overhead. She aborts the recovery. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into certainty that they are not alone, and that the wreck is a trap set long ago.

chapters.title: What Mara Knows
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara's chapter reveals her motive: her father was the Vespera's executive officer, scapegoated alongside Elias Hartwell. She has spent twenty years buying access to records and divers. She also confesses she tipped off no one—but suspects the navy's fixer, Calloway, has been hunting this box since before either woman was born. Emotional beat: rival becomes mirror; two women shaped by the same crime.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Weather turns early and violent. During a second dive in deteriorating conditions, Quentin frees the strongbox just as the storm hits; the boat takes damage, the winch jams, and Suri is nearly lost overboard. They limp toward a sheltered cove with a leaking hull and a box they can't open. Emotional beat: survival instinct overriding everything—the price of the prize made physical.

chapters.title: Calloway
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Stranded in the cove, they're found by Calloway, a navy 'insurance investigator' whose courtesy is a blade. He offers Quentin immunity and a clean identity in exchange for the box and Mara. That night, Quentin opens the box: orders, logs, and a recording proving Elias obeyed lawful commands and was silenced anyway. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare—her old life back, bought with her brother's truth twice buried.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: POV Suri. Through the youngest crew member's eyes, we see the crew fracture: Dov wants to deal, Mara wants to run for international waters, Quentin goes silent. Suri forces the question—what is this crew for?—and Quentin finally answers: each other. They patch the hull through the night while Calloway's cutter waits offshore. Emotional beat: belonging chosen out loud; the crew becomes a decision, not an accident.

chapters.title: Passage
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Climax. Quentin runs the cutter blockade through the storm's worst squall, using the wreck field's submerged hazards against Calloway's larger vessel. Mara sacrifices her father's original documents—scattering them to the sea—to force Calloway to break off and rescue his own drifting boarding party rather than pursue. Emotional beat: fury and clarity; power exposed as something that cannot survive being seen.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: POV Quentin. Resolution. The surviving copies of the record reach a journalist; an inquiry reopens the Vespera case, and Elias's name begins its slow rehabilitation. Mara departs to testify; Quentin stays with Dov and Suri, her real name now known to everyone aboard—and that's the point. Final image: diving open water, measuring life in years at last. Emotional beat: quiet arrival; survival's price paid, belonging claimed.
